modulo-2:
I wrote all five units. "node valida.mjs u6 u7 u8 u9 u10" ends with 0 errors and 0 warnings. I didn't touch src/, valida.mjs or other batches' files.

How I built them: a small script in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-patatino/c3cdb1ae-a2ac-5139-9cd5-18b12af4bc5a/scratchpad/b2/ (build.mjs plus one data file per unit) copies each original exercise and replaces only the translated fields. So every Dutch answer (a, alt, x, say) and every Dutch option is copied exactly from src rather than retyped. The script also stops if a g, tt, h or e field is missing.

Hard exercises: each unit has 2 mc, 2 fill, 2 tr and 2 order, easiest first. They mix the unit's rule with earlier units and use Belgian settings (Gent, Antwerpen, Brussel, het frietkot, Gent-Sint-Pieters). Traps include:
- plural het-words: welke kinderen, onze kinderen;
- "kilo" staying singular after a number;
- "je zus gaat": here je is a possessive, so the -t stays;
- "Neem je je jas": two je in a row;
- dus followed by inversion, and the no-inversion rule after want.

Language doubts and choices:
- **Flemish variants accepted:** "Hoe noemt haar broer" (u8), "pakken de trein" (u7, u10), and "bij / aan het frietkot" alongside "in het frietkot" (u6).
- **Moving a phrase after the infinitive:** in u9 and u10 I accepted "wil vanavond koken voor de kinderen/ons" as correct. I avoided wrong options that rely on "gaan naar X", because that order is common in spoken Belgian Dutch.
- **Inverted answers in earlier units:** u6 and u9 accept inverted answers ("Morgen geven de meisjes…", "Vanavond wil mijn moeder…") even though inversion is taught in u10. They are correct Dutch, and rejecting them would be worse.
- **One question changed:** in u7 the question "Quale domanda è corretta?" was copied from an existing exercise (the validator flagged it), so I reworded it to «Scegli la domanda corretta: «Quando la chiami?»».
- **Tighter English wording:** in u8 I used "What is her brother called?" so that "Wat is de naam van…" isn't a correct answer missing from the list.

Adapting for English speakers: the "typical mistakes" sections of the notes are rewritten for English speakers:
- u6: -s on every plural (boeks).
- u7: looking for a "do" (Doe je…?), Wat heet je.
- u8: "Het is mijn" instead of van mij, hun/hen, zijn also meaning "to be", haar also meaning "her" and "hair".
- u9: the false friend wil vs will, no te after a modal.
- u10: English places "where" before "when", the opposite of Dutch; "want" is a false friend meaning because.

The u8 note is shorter, because "no article before a possessive" and "his/her depends on the owner" are already the same in English. Spelling is American English throughout.

modulo-3:
Il validatore riporta 0 errori e 0 avvisi su u11–u15 (comando: node valida.mjs u11 u12 u13 u14 u15). Non ho toccato src/, valida.mjs né i file degli altri lotti.

Come ho generato i file: con piccoli script Python nella cartella /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-patatino/c3cdb1ae-a2ac-5139-9cd5-18b12af4bc5a/scratchpad/lotto3/ (lib.py più uN.py). Gli script copiano gli esercizi da src e sostituiscono solo q, e, h, tt e g, così le parti in olandese restano identiche per costruzione. Agli esercizi difficili "order" ho aggiunto tt uguale a q, come in out/u10.json, per togliere l'avviso "manca tt".

Esercizi difficili (8 per unità, 2 per tipo). Usano solo regole dell'unità o di quelle precedenti, mai di quelle successive:
- u11 non contiene niet/geen, perché la negazione arriva con u12.
- u12 e u13 non usano aggettivi davanti al nome con la -e, che arrivano con u14.

Trabocchetti principali:
- u11: half twaalf per le 23:40; "jullie winkel sluit", dove il soggetto è il negozio e non jullie.
- u12: "ik heb ze niet", con il pronome si usa niet; niet prima dell'infinito dopo un modale.
- u13: "die glazen", plurale di una het-parola; "Dit zijn de foto's".
- u14: "een koud bier" e "geen groot huis", senza -e; "ons kleine dorp" e "dit witte hemd", con -e.
- u15: "een grotere stad"; "duurder" ma "duurste"; "lekkerder" ma "lekkerste".

Adattamenti per gli anglofoni:
- u11: aggiunto l'avviso che il "half three" britannico vuol dire 3:30, mentre half drie è 2:30.
- u12: geen spiegato come "no / not a / not any"; l'olandese non ha un ausiliare come "do".
- u13: l'errore tipico è "Deze zijn…", calcato su "These are…"; anche "pants" è un plurale come in italiano, mentre de broek è singolare.
- u14: l'aggettivo inglese non cambia mai, quindi l'errore principale diventa dimenticare la -e. Ho tolto l'errore "aggettivo dopo il nome", che per un anglofono non esiste.
- u15: l'inglese usa more/most con gli aggettivi lunghi, l'olandese mai (niente "meer duur"); "als" scambiato per "than"; "dan ik" contro l'inglese "than me".
- Ho usato l'inglese americano: pants, movie, apartment, gray.

Dubbi linguistici:
- u12, tr "Oggi mia sorella non va a Gand in treno": tra le risposte ho messo anche l'ordine "niet naar Gent met de trein".
- u15, fill "het mooist": accetto anche "mooiste".
- u15, tr "più economici di quelli": accetto "dan die", "dan die broek" e "dan die daar".
- u14 hard[5] (order): come alternativa accetto anche l'ordine inverso "een witte kat en een zwarte hond".
- u15: ho evitato apposta "dan mij" / "dan ik" nelle opzioni, perché è una forma discussa in olandese.
- I suggerimenti h che erano aggettivi olandesi base (rood, mooi, koud…) sono rimasti in olandese, come nell'originale.

frasi-mazzi:
Both files written and validated: "node valida.mjs ordersets" and "node valida.mjs decks" each report 0 errors and 0 warnings. src/, valida.mjs and other batches' files were not touched.

ordersets.json: all 14 series have 10 sentences each, in the original order. Each series has t, s and rule; each sentence has it and e. Dutch inside <i> and <b> is unchanged. The English sentences follow the Dutch solution a/alt:
- mogen is translated "be allowed to" (for example "You're allowed to park here"), not "can", so kunnen can't also look right.
- "(formal)" is added where the answer only has u (subfirst[6]).
- In q[8], "you (all)" marks jullie.
- want/omdat keep the comma vs no-comma pair from the Italian, since English uses "because" for both.
- rel[9] is kept as a restrictive clause with no commas, to match the Dutch.
- Place names use English forms: Ghent, Brussels, Antwerp, Bruges. Leuven stays Leuven.

The comparisons with Italian were rewritten for English speakers. New points include: no do-support in questions and with niet, no -ing form, time–manner–place being the reverse of English order, dat and die/dat not being droppable as they are in English, and modal + infinitive not staying together.

The extra field "unit" was not repeated, following the format in the brief.

decks.json: all 19 decks have the same cards in the same order, and column 0 is identical.
- dehet: only the meaning was translated ("the house", and so on).
- Decks with sayExtra (irr1, irr2, sep, prep): the Dutch detail is unchanged.
- opp and vlaams: the detail was translated ("In the Netherlands: …").
- I also added a translated "g" field to each deck (Grammar / Vocabulary / Flemish). It is extra and the integrator can ignore it.

Spelling and wording choices:
- American English throughout (store, color, neighbor, fall/autumn, restroom, subway/metro).
- Ambiguous words get double glosses: vriend = friend/boyfriend, neef = cousin (m.)/nephew, tuin = garden/yard, bakker = baker/bakery.
- Distinctions Italian marks that English doesn't are made explicit: liggen "to lie (be lying down)" vs liegen "to lie (tell a lie)", and weten "to know (a fact)".

Language doubts:
- "Het vriest" is given as "It's freezing." (literally "it's below zero").
- "ziek zijn" in the work deck is "to be off sick".
- "het verlof" is "the leave, the vacation days".
